sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (federal common-law jurisdiction with civil law governing private and commercial matters in Quebec)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (entered into force 1 October 2014)
United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA/CUSMA) (entered into force 1 July 2020)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) (provisionally applicable since 21 September 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal AML/CTF: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and its regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46 (proceeds of crime and terrorist-financing provisions); FINTRAC regulatory guidance. Provincial registration and UBO context: Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises (LPE), CQLR c. P-44.1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2186 et seq. (partnerships) and arts. 2236 et seq. (limited partnership / societe en commandite). Quebec does not maintain a public beneficial-ownership register for limited partnerships; beneficial ownership of limited partners is private/internal and is primarily documented through FINTRAC-regulated financial intermediaries. FINTRAC, CRA, Sirete du Quebec and other authorities may obtain UBO information pursuant to lawful process and AML/CTF investigative powers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of current passport or government-issued photo identification of each individual general partner; for any limited partner holding 25% or more of the partnership, a notarized passport copy is also required for the UBO file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin; apostille issued by the designated competent authority in that state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the source state is party to the Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization by a Canadian consulate or embassy in the source state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official corporate registry extract for any entity acting as a general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or trade/company registrar of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization by Canadian authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolutions or power of attorney authorizing execution of the Quebec limited partnership agreement and the declaration of registration (immatriculation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public in the source jurisdiction verifying due authorization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French corporate records, identification documents, and supporting corporate resolutions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator affiliated with the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator certification accompanied by apostilled/consular-legalized source documents; register acceptance governed by the LPE and the Charter of the French Language

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation and at each UBO change, all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more of economic or voting interests, and authorized signatories must be screened against: the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; Canada's Listed Terrorist Entities list under section 83.05 of the Criminal Code; the U.S. OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; and the EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. Politically exposed person (PEP) determination follows the PCMLTFA Regulations (SOR/2002-184) definitions for domestic, foreign, and international PEPs, including heads of state/government, ministers, senior military officials, judges, and central bank officials. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign PEPs, high-risk jurisdictional links, and any sanctioned counterparty. Screening results, UBO ownership matrices, and source-of-wealth evidence must be documented and retained for at least five years in accordance with PCMLTFA record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) - official online portal: https://www.registraire.gouv.qc.ca ; name reservation and related searches are performed through the Registraire's online services ('Services en ligne').
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises, the corporate name must be in French. A name in another language is accepted only if a French version is provided and becomes the registered legal name, unless a recognized trademark exception applies. Non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters in the French legal name. The Registraire applies the linguistic and typographical standards of the Office quebecois de la langue francaise, including capitalization, accents, and acceptable abbreviations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gouvernement, Ministere, Municipal, Public, Royal, Reine, Couronne, Souverain (terms implying governmental, sovereign, or municipal authority)

Avocat, Notaire, Barreau, Conseil (as professionals), Comptable, Auditeur, Banque, Banquier, Assurance, Fiducie, Trust, Bourse (regulated or self-regulating professions and financial activities requiring special ministerial or professional authorization)
Universite, College, Ordre professionnel (terms implying educational or professional accreditation without prior approval)
Obscene, scandalous, misleading, or otherwise contrary to public order or public morality terms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is refused, the Registraire issues a written refusal notice identifying the statutory basis and, where applicable, the conflicting registered name. The applicant may (i) file an immediate reservation of a revised name; or (ii) submit a written administrative review request within 30 days of notification, addressing the stated grounds and providing evidence of trademark registration, prior ministerial approval, or reduced likelihood of confusion. If the administrative review is denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Court of Quebec, civil division, within 30 days of the final refusal, pursuant to the Code of Civil Procedure and the Act respecting administrative justice. For a valid reservation approaching expiry, the applicant may seek a 90-day renewal during the reservation period; if the reservation expires without use, a new name search and reservation application must be started.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for a Print-on-Demand retail limited partnership only if the virtual office provider maintains a physical civic address in Quebec, is staffed during normal business hours, and is authorized to accept service of process and registered mail. A post office box or a remote virtual-only address without local service capacity is prohibited. The partnership's declaration of registration must show a real geolocatable address in Quebec where the partnership's books, records, and the limited partnership agreement may be inspected or produced when required. Because the business is digital-only and low-risk, a commercial registered-office or serviced-office arrangement at an active Quebec street address is acceptable to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very Low (below 5% annual probability) for a low-risk, cashless, online e-commerce LP with a complete AML/UBO file and compliant filings. The likelihood escalates to 25-50% if annual registration declarations are missed, FINTRAC/CRA compliance queries arise, a suspicious transaction report is filed, or PEP/sanctions red flags are triggered.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec name availability search and name reservation (single name) through the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set out in the regulation respecting fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises; online application rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial registration of the Quebec limited partnership (declaration of immatriculation / declaration of registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff for a limited partnership; no minimum capital requirement applies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille / consular legalization, and certified true copies of foreign partner identification and corporate records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in source jurisdiction and source-state Apostille Competent Authority or Canadian consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing foreign notarial, apostille, and consular fee schedule; not a Quebec statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: OTTIAQ-certified French translation of all foreign-language identification, corporate documents, and resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: OTTIAQ professional benchmark rate per source document; estimated for a standard cross-border LP file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing and AML/KYC screening file: ownership matrix, 25% threshold analysis, PEP and sanctions screening, and source-of-wealth verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML/KYC compliance provider or Quebec law firm engaged in the pre-incorporation review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market professional benchmark for a low-risk retail UBO dossier, approximately 2-3 hours of senior analyst time

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and review of the Quebec limited partnership agreement, declaration of registration, and pre-incorporation governance advice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec law firm (Barreau du Quebec) or notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing legal market rate for cross-border e-commerce limited partnership formation, approximately 5-7 hours at CAD 150-250 per hour converted to USD

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ) arts. 2236-2262 (Société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1) arts. 2-14, 33-38; Regulation respecting the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (c. P-44.1, r. 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Enterprise Registration and Legal Publicity Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) for a limited partnership (société en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under Quebec law. Contributions are fixed in the limited partnership agreement; no escrow account or capitalization declaration is required at registration. The general partner must hold at least one partnership unit, and non-resident limited partners are permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned general partner, acting as manager of the limited partnership, approves the subscription and acceptance of partnership units in the capital of the limited partnership by each subscriber as set forth in the limited partnership agreement; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the limited partnership is established at its proposed address in Quebec, until changed by proper resolution; RESOLVED, that the authorized representative is appointed as chief corporate officer with the authority to sign and file the Declaration of Registration and any other instruments required under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; all actions taken pursuant to these resolutions are hereby ratified and approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online Centre d'affaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name search in the REQ enterprise register to ensure the proposed limited partnership name is distinct and lawful. File an online name reservation request providing up to three proposed names. Upon approval, retain the certificate of reservation for use in the Declaration of Registration.
required_dossiers: General partner identification (natural person: date of birth and Quebec home address; legal person: enterprise identifier or registration number)
Summary of activities for name screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised name request in writing to REQ within 10 days; no new filing fee is charged if filed under the same inquiry; otherwise pay the standard name reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and signature of limited partnership agreement and registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary in Quebec (Chambre des notaires du Québec) / REQ for form content
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a consensual limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) specifying the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, profit sharing, and management powers. Complete the Declaration of Registration form (available on REQ's website), listing the partnership name, registered office, partners, authorized representatives, and business activities. Have the signatures attested or notarized as required, and obtain identity attestation for each partner.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (privately signed with attested signatures or notarized)
Draft Declaration of Registration (REQ form or online equivalent)
Notarial attestation or witnessed signature page
Power of attorney if signing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ identifies missing attestations, file a corrective declaration with a sworn statement within 15 days; if the underlying contract fails to satisfy legal publicity requirements, restate the declaration and pay the applicable correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration and issuance of Quebec enterprise number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online submission portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into REQ's online registration system, complete the declaration fields exactly as set out in the approved form, attach the required supporting dossiers, and pay the filing fee by credit card. Submit the declaration. Within the statutory processing period, REQ will issue a certificate of registration, the enterprise number (NEQ), and an extract from the enterprise register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence for a corporate general partner, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by REQ (avis de défaut), provide a corrective declaration or supporting evidence within 30 days; if the defect is material and not cured, REQ may refuse, and the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Court of Québec within 60 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secondary registrations: Revenu Québec, CRA, and municipal permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (RQ); Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued NEQ and registration certificate, register with Revenu Québec for a Quebec employer account, QST, and tax deduction accounts, and with the CRA for GST/HST and partnership income tax reporting. Apply to the local municipality for an occupancy permit and a commercial licence if a physical establishment is used. Confirm that municipal zoning permits a light commercial POD operation with retail sales.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of REQ registration extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or municipal application is rejected, respond to the notice with corrected addresses or a revised business classification within the deadline stated in the notice, generally 30 days; for zoning refusals, file an exclusion request with the municipal review committee and, if necessary, appeal to the competent administrative tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Service de l'aménagement et du développement économique de la localité (municipal urbanism and economic development office)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d'occupation / Permis de commerce pour exploitation légère (Print-on-Demand workshop retail)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction régionale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory full EIA for this low-volume, light industrial commercial activity; subject to the Registration category only if pollutant discharge thresholds are exceeded; otherwise addressed through municipal bylaw compliance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must conform to municipal sewer by-laws (suspended solids ≤ 15 mg/L, 5-day BOD ≤ 10 mg/L) and, if released to a sanitary sewer, to the Quebec municipal sewage works regulations; VOC emissions from inks and heat-press operations must comply with section 20 of the Environmental Quality Act and the Regulation respecting the quality of the atmosphere, including odour nuisance limits and concentration thresholds set in any local emission certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire safety service under the Fire Safety Act and the National Building Code of Canada; structural load inspection and verification if printing equipment is installed in a multi-storey building; occupational health and safety clearance from CNESST for equipment guarding, ventilation, and hazardous products storage under the applicable Quebec safety codes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal GST/HST and income tax administration, through the Business Registration Online portal and CRA My Business Account; and Revenu Québec — provincial QST and Quebec income tax administration, through the Revenu Québec online business portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Québec limited partnership (LP): (i) verify whether the LP is 'carrying on business in Canada' and whether the CAD $30,000 small-supplier threshold has been crossed; (ii) obtain a 15-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA using Form RC1 or Business Registration Online; (iii) register for the federal GST/HST account under the BN, and register for the QST account with Revenu Québec (BN suffix PQ, using the Revenu Québec registration form LM-1-V); (iv) where no Canadian presence exists, designate a Canadian representative for service and tax communication and expect possible security or bond requirements under ETA section 300; (v) register the partnership itself as the GST/HST/QST registrant, but treat income as flowing through to partners. File the T5013 Partnership Information Return with the CRA and the corresponding Revenu Québec partnership information return where required; each partner reports its allocated share of Canadian business income in its own jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box election. An LP is treated as a fiscally transparent partnership for Canadian income tax; no election is available to tax it as a corporation. For GST/QST, the LP is a taxable person separate from its partners. Income allocations may be set in the partnership agreement but must reflect the partners' entitlement to partnership profits under the Income Tax Act. Unpaid current allocations may create hybrid mismatch exposure under Canada's anti-hybrid rules; no statutory election can cure that misalignment. The sole relevant sales-tax election is voluntary registration as a small supplier or non-resident supplier.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal, 5%) + Québec QST (provincial, 9.975% calculated on the selling price before GST); combined non-harmonized headline levy: 14.975%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 of worldwide taxable supply consideration (excluding sales tax) made by the LP together with associated persons in any four consecutive calendar quarters; this threshold applies to both the GST/HST (CRA) and the QST (Revenu Québec) and triggers mandatory registration and tax collection once exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, API stamping, or electronic-invoicing clearance mandate currently applies in Canada or Québec. Businesses must issue invoices or simplified sales vouchers for taxable supplies and retain all records, including electronic records, for six years. EDI/PDF invoices are accepted if they contain the required information and are legible and auditable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered GST/HST-QST supplier may zero-rate the POD custom apparel supply when it exports the goods from Canada to a destination outside Canada, provided the LP holds reliable evidence of physical export. The design/printing service and the custom merchandise are treated as one composite zero-rated supply of goods if the service is incidental/ancillary to and charged with the exported goods. Export zero-rating applies to GST and QST; the LP can then claim input tax credits/refunds for GST and QST paid on Canadian inputs within the standard substantiation rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A or courier/customs-broker equivalent) where the export exceeds the reporting threshold
Commercial invoice containing the foreign customer name, foreign address, item description, consideration, and HS classification
Bill of lading, air waybill, or postal/courier shipment receipt showing dispatch from Canada
Third-party proof of delivery outside Canada: foreign customs entry, delivery confirmation from carrier, or foreign border crossing stamp
Payment record from the foreign buyer (Stripe/PayPal settlement, SWIFT/remittance, or card acquirer record)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no statutory export-fx repatriation deadline; the zero-rating condition is physical export plus documentary proof. If the CRA or Revenu Québec later disallows the zero rating, the LP is assessed for uncollected GST/QST, compound daily interest, and penalties under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec Tax Administration Act (failure to file, false statements, gross negligence). Fraudulent zero-rating claims can lead to criminal prosecution, seizure of records, and monetary fines. The six-year record-retention requirement must be respected; the normal reassessment period for GST/HST is four years but is extended for misrepresentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); FX administration and monetary policy under the Bank of Canada Act; AML/ATF transaction surveillance by FINTRAC; prudential oversight of financial institutions by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); Quebec financial-sector licensing (when applicable) by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital account; Canada operates an independent floating exchange-rate regime with no general exchange-control legislation requiring government approval for conversion or remittance. Profit distributions, capital repatriation and liquidation proceeds may be converted and remitted freely to non-resident limited partners. Convertibility is enshrined by Canada's OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements and CUSMA obligations. Banking frictions are documentary only: financial institutions must perform customer due diligence (CDD) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and file FINTRAC reports for electronic funds transfers (EFT) of CAD 10,000 or more.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, conversion or repatriation timeline for export receipts; the LP may freely retain POD sales revenue in CAD or foreign currency. For income tax purposes, subsection 39(1) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the equivalent Quebec Taxation Act provisions require foreign-currency gains and losses to be measured in CAD using the Bank of Canada noon or daily average exchange rate; GST/HST and QST returns likewise convert foreign sales into Canadian dollars per published CRA/Revenu Québec rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Core corporate operating account (CAD) with a linked USD clearing sub-account for cross-border POD settlement
Business operating account and commercial deposit account for the LP (compte d'exploitation); treasury services via Desjardins Capital Markets
CAD operating account + USD cross-border treasury account (BMO Harris Bank correspondent channel) for export proceeds invoicing

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Small-business operational account with e-commerce settlement capability
Corporate settlement account with FXOnline and RBC Express clearing tools

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EMI rails that operate through a regulated Canadian partner bank (e.g., Stripe Treasury, Wise Business, or Airwallex gateway clearing into a Schedule I bank account); Low for purely offshore digital EMIs lacking a Canadian branch or FINTRAC money-service-business (MSB) registration. Legal constraints: an offshore EMI processing CAD settlement or executing customer wires for the LP without either (i) FINTRAC MSB registration in Canada or (ii) an exemption under section 8 of the PCMLTFA would be non-compliant and would be refused by the onboarding bank as a circular-payments counterparty. Recommended architecture: use EMIs solely as an e-commerce collection conduit to the LP's Schedule I CAD/USD accounts; execute all supplier disbursements and FX through the chartered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec limited partnership, the natural-person directors of the corporate general partner and the designated senior officer must complete an in-person identification interview at a commercial banking centre in Montreal (or an equivalent approved virtual KYC interview with notarized photo identification). Remote opening is permitted for a Low_Risk_Standard online-retail business where the bank can verify identity through a recognized digital credential (Verified.Me / Interac) and receive a notarized true copy of the partnership's immatriculation certificate from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ). If any limited partner is a non-Canadian entity, the bank will additionally require an apostilled certificate of status, a legal opinion on the partner's authority, and a copy of the LP's beneficial-ownership register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value e-commerce settlement pattern (Stripe/PayPal) resembling money movement and potentially an unregistered money-services-business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-processor settlement statements (Stripe and PayPal); e-commerce store transaction logs; order-level shipping records (Canada Post, UPS, FedEx); the marketplace/mobile-app agreement; and a written attestation that receipts are proceeds of physical custom-merchandise sales, not money transmission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of LP beneficial ownership with non-resident limited partners and no minimum compulsory capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Limited partnership agreement; Quebec beneficial-ownership register extract (Registraire des entreprises); passport and proof-of-address for every partner holding 25% or more; REQ certificate of immatriculation; and an authorization resolution of the general partner appointing the account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border print-on-demand supplier chain touching U.S. and China, exposing the account to trade-based money-laundering typologies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed POD supplier and fulfillment agreements; CBSA customs entry documents (Form B3 / CADEX) with HS codes; supplier invoices containing product identification, unit price and shipment incoterms; and a bank-traversable reconciliation of purchase orders to inventory dispatches.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated chargeback and refund velocity creating a circular-refund or credit-balance-laundering red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Published refund and returns policy; processor chargeback reports; refund journal entries traced to the original card or wallet; historical settlement-to-refund reconciliation; and six months of bank statements demonstrating that refunds are never re-routed to third-party accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online retail classified as non-store retail trade (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110) with insufficient physical substance or inventory for an LP domiciled in Quebec
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: REQ certificate of immatriculation; lease or virtual-office subscription with a Quebec address; statutory declaration describing the e-commerce storefront; print-on-demand platform agreements; and an external negative-media / sanctions search for all partners and directors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) foreign limited partner originates an SWIFT MT103 with value date T+1 to the LP's Canadian operating account via the partner's bank; (ii) wire narrative must state 'Capital contribution — LP agreement dated [date], partner No. [N]'; (iii) the receiving bank applies standard PCMLTFA CDD — an electronic funds transfer (EFT) report is filed with FINTRAC for any single transaction of CAD 10,000 or more; (iv) no exchange-control permit is required for inbound CAD or USD; (v) for contributions exceeding CAD 100,000 the bank's corporate AML desk may request the LP's audited capital-account statement, the REQ beneficial-ownership extract and a confirmatory resolution of the general partner; (vi) inbound USD is converted to CAD at the closing spot rate unless a USD clearing sub-account is maintained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursement rails: (i) domestic CAD supplier and salary payments via Payments Canada (ACSS or the Real-Time Rail) using direct credits from the LP's operating account; (ii) cross-border supplier wires (U.S. and Asia) executed as SWIFT MT103 through the Canadian bank's correspondent network (e.g., BMO via BMO Harris New York/Fedwire); (iii) for bulk purchase of print blanks or garment stock, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (commercial L/C) with the vendor bank as advising and paying bank; (iv) Stripe/PayPal daily settlement batches are swept into the LP's CAD or USD account through processor ACH/automated clearing to the designated depository; (v) FX conversion of USD export proceeds to CAD is delivered through the bank's FX desk or electronic dealing platform before supplier disbursement, with conversion records retained for income-tax and QST audit trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD vanilla FX forward contracts (maturity 1-12 months) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA with a Schedule I Canadian bank treasury desk — permissible to lock conversion of USD-denominated POD export receivables; the notional must not exceed 120% of reasonably forecast USD gateway settlements, and speculative rollover is prohibited.

FX swaps (swap of principal with same value date) used to provide temporary CAD funding for supplier disbursements against incoming USD settlement liquidity — permissible when each leg is tied to an identifiable invoice or settlement batch.

OTC vanilla CAD/USD call and put options (premium-based) hedging asymmetric exposure on large seasonal POD licensing or bulk-manufacturing payments — permissible under the bank's derivatives authorization for plain-vanilla products and capped at 120% of the underlying commercial exposure.

Cross-currency swap (CAD floating for USD fixed) permissible for long-term USD-denominated supplier finance or intercompany loan capital exceeding CAD 250,000, provided it is executed with the treasury desk and documented by a business-purpose statement.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) — structurally permissible in Canada only where the CAD leg cannot be physically settled offshore and the bank uses the Reuters CAD reference rate as the fixing source; for a domestic Quebec LP this is non-market standard because CAD is freely deliverable, and a covered deliverable forward is the efficient compliant alternative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Updating Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (LPE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise's initial registration; if the anniversary falls on a non-business day, the deadline extends to the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts fixed penalties up to $100 per day (minimum $100, maximum $1,000). Persistent non-filing for more than 24 months triggers administrative strike-off (radiation), with loss of the limited-liability shield for existing limited partners and inhibition of the partnership's capacity to maintain judicial actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal) and associated financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a calendar-year period ending December 31, the return is due by May 31, and T5013 slips must be furnished to each partner by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of $25 per partner per day, with a minimum of $100 and a maximum of $2,500 per return; continued default may lead to criminal prosecution and gross-negligence penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Provincial Partnership Information Return and RL-15 Relevés de renseignements (Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a calendar-year partnership, TP-600 is due by May 31, and RL-15 slips must be issued to each partner by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of $25 per day (minimum $100, maximum $2,500) under the Taxation Act; failure to provide an RL-15 slip triggers a per-slip penalty of $30, subject to aggregate minimums and maximums up to $2,500.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit exists for a privately-held limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An independent audit becomes compulsory only when the partnership is a reporting issuer or an investment fund under Canadian securities legislation, or when the partnership agreement or a lender/institutional investor covenant expressly requires an audited financial statement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for reporting issuers or entities subject to public accountability; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for a typical closed limited partnership engaged in Print-on-Demand retail; Quebec tax accounting rules also govern income computation for provincial purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec LPE requires an annual updating declaration confirming the identity and residential address of each general and limited partner, together with the designated partner for service. Transfers of partnership interests are reflected by amending the public declaration and the private partnership register; no separate UBO register applies because a limited partnership is not a legal person under Quebec civil law. All register entries, contribution records, and transfer documentation must be retained for at least seven years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Limited Partners (name, address, contribution, share, transfer date)
Partnership Minute Book (general partner resolutions and consents)
General Ledger, journal, and supporting contemporaneous books (Art. 2240 C.C.Q.)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required unless stipulated by contract or regulatory status; typical certified audit fee for a small POD limited partnership: $3,500 - $7,500
